Irene / Ben —

Reviewed Jack's redline. Below is a proposal we can send back to Stratus that balances defense obligations with reasonable operational limits and risk allocation. I'll send a tracked redline if you want to use it verbatim, but here are the key points we should offer: 

1) Scope of indemnity (third-party IP claims): Redwood will indemnify and defend Customer (Stratus) against third-party claims to the extent the claim arises from (i) Redwood's model architecture or training artifacts that Redwood controls, or (ii) defects in Redwood's hosted serving infrastructure. We should expressly exclude: (a) Customer content (prompts, uploads, connectors), (b) open-source components where liability arises from upstream licensor obligations, and (c) claims based solely on Customer's manner of use or prompt engineering.

2) Defense control / settlement consent: Redwood will have the right to assume defense with counsel of its choosing. Stratus may participate at its own counsel expense. Redwood will not settle any claim that admits fault or imposes an ongoing obligation on Stratus without Stratus's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld). If Redwood declines defense, Stratus may assume control and Redwood will reimburse reasonable defense costs up to the indemnity cap (see below).

3) Evidence custody & preservation: We'll commit to preserve service-side artifacts reasonably requested to investigate a claim for a 90-day preservation window following written notice, limited to artifacts that Redwood routinely retains (request examples: model id & version, request id, hashed prompt metadata, policy-allowed KV cache snapshots). We will not provide raw customer prompt content or proprietary customer data without a lawful basis. Operationally, any preservation beyond routine retention (e.g., snapshot restore or forensic extraction) will be chargeable at our then-current support rates and subject to a separate statement of work.

4) Caps / insurance offset: Indemnity will be subject to an aggregate cap equal to the fees paid under the Order Form for the preceding 12 months (or $X, whichever is greater). Insurance offsets and subrogation will be handled per our standard MSA clause.

5) Evidence handling & chain of custody: We'll propose an SOC-2 style evidence transfer checklist and an NDA addendum for any forensic artifacts transferred to Stratus's counsel. This protects sensitive logs and ensures redactions where necessary.

If you want, I'll attach a tracked redline (changes to the MSA/Order Form) and a short two-slide MAP describing timings: 1) technical call to agree evidence items (2 business days), 2) legal finalization (2-3 business days), 3) signatures.

Two operational notes for Ben: if preservation requests are likely to include large KV cache dumps or require SRE intervention, we should flag estimated hours now so procurement can budget.

Kimberly
